task: Predict energy consumed during the next complete hour in kWh
primary_research_question: Can a compact model prepared for edge deployment reduce next-hour energy forecast error against a 24-hour mean baseline and support conditional depletion warnings when starting balance is known?
hypothesis: Selected ML model reduces held-out next-hour MAE by at least 10 percent relative to the 24-hour mean baseline; this is a predeclared practical target, not an assumed result.
raw_source: UCI Individual Household Electric Power Consumption, DOI 10.24432/C58K54
split: First 70 percent of hourly timeline train, next 15 percent validation, final 15 percent test. No shuffle. Label hours do not overlap.
selection: Select configuration and model family using validation MAE only; refit the winner on train plus validation, then evaluate frozen models on the held-out test.

secondary_scenarios.labels: Assigned starting balances combined with measured held-out consumption. These are constructed scenarios, not observed prepaid meter depletion events.
secondary_scenarios.within_hour_assumption: Uniform consumption in the exhaustion hour
